[ASSISTANT_SAID] The digestive system is made up of various organs that work together to break down food into nutrients and eliminate waste from the body.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Major features and functions of the digestive system include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Mouth: Breaks down food into smaller pieces by chewing and mixes it with saliva containing enzymes that begin to break down carbohydrates.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Esophagus: A muscular tube that connects the mouth to the stomach, using muscle contractions to move food down.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Stomach: Secretes digestive juices containing hydrochloric acid and enzymes that break down proteins, mixing and grinding food into chyme.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Small intestine: Primary site for nutrient absorption, where digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats is completed with the help of enzymes from the pancreas and liver.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Large intestine: Absorbs water and electrolytes from chyme, forming solid waste to be eliminated as feces.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A healthy digestive system is essential for overall health and well-being, helping maintain a healthy weight, providing energy, and supporting the immune system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Digestive health has been linked to mental health and inflammation control.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Adequate fiber, hydration, and a balanced diet support optimal digestive function.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for improving digestive health include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Eat a balanced diet rich in whole foods like fruits, vegetables, grains, legumes, and lean proteins.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Stay hydrated by drinking enough water to prevent constipation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Practice mindful eating by eating slowly and chewing thoroughly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Engage in regular exercise to reduce inflammation and keep the digestive tract moving.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Manage stress through relaxation techniques like meditation, yoga, or deep breathing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Include prebiotic-rich foods (e.g., bananas, artichokes, onions, asparagus) and probiotic-rich foods (e.g., kefir, kimchi, yogurt) in your diet.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Consult with a healthcare provider if symptoms persist.
